description: Phase 6bt (post-9be persistence gate) — INSERTs into an indexed table must flush populated 0x0a index-leaf pages on db_close, not empty ones. Regression for the 2026-04-20 silent file-format-compat bug: leap-c serialised an empty 0x0a page for every index regardless of ie->cells_n, so the index was dropped at close-time. leap-c read its own DB via table scan (planner didn't consult the index for single-table ORDER BY scans), masking the corruption. Mainline SQLite, which DID use the index, saw zero rows and PRAGMA integrity_check reported 'wrong # of entries in index'. Fixtures validate that a leap-c-written DB with a populated index is well-formed per mainline (integrity_check 'ok') and returns the expected rows via mainline's index-based planner.

case.name: string — unique
case.ddl: string — DDL to create schema (table + index)
case.inserts: array of strings — INSERT statements run in order inside a single BEGIN/COMMIT
case.expect_integrity_ok: boolean — mainline PRAGMA integrity_check must return 'ok'
case.select_index_ordered: string — SELECT that exercises the index path (e.g. ORDER BY indexed col)
case.expect_rows_ordered: array of arrays — rows the SELECT must return, in order

cases.name: index-persist-single-row
cases.description: CREATE TABLE + CREATE INDEX + 1 INSERT + ORDER BY indexed col must return the row. Reproduces the original bug report: schema=indexed-text, rowcount=1.
cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE kv (k TEXT, v TEXT); CREATE INDEX idx_k ON kv(k);
cases.select_index_ordered: SELECT k FROM kv ORDER BY k;

cases.name: index-persist-hundred-rows
cases.description: 100 rows through the same shape — cells fit on a single 0x0a leaf (no Phase 9d split needed).
cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE kv (k TEXT, v INTEGER); CREATE INDEX kv_k ON kv(k);

cases.name: index-persist-reopen
cases.description: Persist-and-reopen via CLI (leap-c writes, closes, reopens, SELECTs). Validates that (a) the populated 0x0a leaf round-trips through db_close / db_open, and (b) the reopened index still drives leap-c's own ORDER BY traversal correctly.
cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE kv (k TEXT, v INTEGER); CREATE INDEX kv_k ON kv(k);
cases.select_index_ordered: SELECT k, v FROM kv ORDER BY k;

cases.name: index-persist-10k-split
cases.description: Phase 9d regression: n=10000 rows spill the index past a single 0x0a leaf. leap-c's writer must split cells across multiple leaves + build a 0x02 interior root (reusing sqlite_schema.rootpage). Mainline must integrity_check to 'ok' and read the rows in index order. This is the C-side analog of roundtrip_index_paging.py's `write-large-indexed-roundtrip` case (which exercises leap-rust).
cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE kv (k TEXT, v INTEGER); CREATE INDEX kv_k ON kv(k);

cases.name: index-persist-10k-reopen
cases.description: Phase 9d regression with reopen_between: after leap-c writes 10k rows + splits the index, leap-c re-opens the DB and must walk the 0x02 root + 0x0a leaves (read_index_tree / walk_index_tree_page) to rebuild the in-memory IndexEntry.cells before the table-ordered SELECT. This is the C-side analog of `read-large-indexed-from-mainline`, but with self-read instead of mainline-produced input.
cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE kv (k TEXT, v INTEGER); CREATE INDEX kv_k ON kv(k);
cases.select_index_ordered: SELECT k, v FROM kv ORDER BY k LIMIT 5;
